983: Narrated Jabir (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the selling of fruits until they were ripe, and that nothing of it should be sold except for dinars and dirhams, except in the case of 'Araya.
978: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The two parties to a sale have the option (of canceling it) so long as they have not separated, unless it is a sale with an option (specified)."
1008: Narrated Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Procrastination (delay) in payment by a wealthy person is injustice (oppression). So if the debt of any one of you is transferred from his debtor to a rich person, he should agree."
1022: Narrated Abu Al-Minhal: I asked Al-Bara' bin 'Azib and Zaid bin Arqam about As-Sarf (money exchange), and each of them would say, "This one is better than me." But both of them said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade selling gold for silver on credit.
1023: Narrated Abu Bakrah (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the exchange of silver for silver, and gold for gold, unless it was equal for equal, and he commanded us to buy gold with silver however we wished, and to buy silver with gold however we wished.
1003: Narrated 'Aishah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) heard the voice of two disputants at the door, their voices being raised, and one of them was asking the other to reduce (something owed to him) and to be lenient with him regarding some matter, while the other was saying: "By Allah, I will not do it." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came out to them and said: "Where is the one who swears by Allah that he will not do a good deed?" The man said: "I am he, O Messenger of Allah, and he may have whichever of the two he prefers."
986: Narrated Sahl bin Abi Hathmah: That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the sale of fresh fruit for dried dates, but he permitted the sale of the 'Ariyah, that it may be sold by estimation, so that its people could eat it as fresh dates.
967: Narrated Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade two ways of dressing and two types of sale: he forbade al-Mulamasah and al-Munabadhah in sale. Al-Mulamasah is when a man touches the garment of another with his hand, by night or by day, without turning it over except by that touch. Al-Munabadhah is when a man throws his garment to another man, and the other throws his garment, and that constitutes their sale, without examination or mutual consent. As for the two ways of dressing: [one is] Ishtimal as-Samma', and as-Samma' is when a man places his garment over one of his shoulders, so that one of his sides is exposed, having no garment over it. The other manner of dressing is his wrapping himself in his garment while sitting, with nothing covering his private parts.
1051: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Al-'Umra (a gift of lifelong usufruct) is permissible."
1067: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: He caught up with 'Umar bin Al-Khattab while he was among a group of riders, and he was swearing by his father. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called out to them: "Behold! Allah forbids you to swear by your fathers. Whoever wishes to swear, let him swear by Allah, or else let him remain silent."
1057: Narrated Talhah bin Musarrif: I asked 'Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, "Did the Prophet (ﷺ) make a will?" He said, "No." I said, "How is it then that making a will has been enjoined on the Muslims, or that they have been ordered to make wills?" He said, "He made a will concerning the Book of Allah."
1080: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "A righteous slave has a double reward." By Him in Whose Hand my soul is, were it not for Jihad in the way of Allah, and Hajj, and kindness to my mother, I would have loved to die while I was a slave.
1024: Narrated Abu Sa'eed Al-Khudri and Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) appointed a man over Khaibar, and he brought him some Janib (superior quality) dates. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Are all the dates of Khaibar like this?" He said: "No, by Allah, O Messenger of Allah! We take a Sa' of these for two Sa's, and two Sa's for three." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not do that. Sell the mixed dates for money (Dirhams), and then buy Janib with the money."
1084: Narrated Jabir: A man from among the Ansar declared that his slave would be free after his death (Mudabbar), and he had no other property besides him. This news reached the Prophet (ﷺ) and he said: "Who will buy him from me?" So Nu'aim bin An-Nahham bought him for eight hundred dirhams.
1032: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) demanding payment of a debt, and he spoke harshly. The Companions intended to deal with him (harshly), but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Leave him, for the one who has a right has a right to speak." Then he said: "Give him a camel of the same age as his." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we can only find one better than his." He said: "Give it to him, for the best among you is he who discharges his debt in the best manner."
1099: Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah curses a thief who steals an egg and thus his hand is cut off, and who steals a rope and thus his hand is cut off."
1135: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) named war as deceit.
1136: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Do not wish to meet the enemy, but when you meet them, be steadfast."
1130: Narrated Abu Burdah: The Prophet (ﷺ) sent his grandfather Abu Musa and Mu'adh to Yemen and said, "Make things easy (for the people) and do not make it difficult for them, and give them glad tidings and do not repel them, and be in mutual agreement (cooperate with each other) and do not differ."
1143: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to give an extra share of the booty to some of those whom he sent out on military expeditions, for themselves specially, apart from the share of the whole army.
1105: Narrated Ash-Shaibani: I asked 'Abdullah bin Abi Awfa, "Did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stone (the adulterer)?" He said, "Yes." I asked, "Was it before Surat An-Nur was revealed or after it?" He said, "I do not know."
1137: Narrated 'Abdullah bin Abi Aufa: He wrote to 'Umar bin 'Ubaidullah, when the latter set out to fight the Haruriyya (Khawarij), that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), on one of the days when he met the enemy, waited till the sun had declined, then he stood up among the people and said: "O people! Do not wish to meet the enemy, and ask Allah for safety, but if you meet them, then be patient, and know that Paradise is under the shades of swords." Then he said: "O Allah, Revealer of the Book, Setter in motion of the clouds, Defeater of the confederates, defeat them and grant us victory over them."
1210: Narrated Usaid bin Hudair: A man from the Ansar said, "O Messenger of Allah, will you not employ me as you employed so-and-so?" He (the Prophet ﷺ) said, "You will meet after me [a time of] favoritism (i.e., others being preferred over you), so be patient until you meet me at the Hawd (the Reservoir)."
1217: Narrated Salamah bin Al-Akwa': He entered upon Al-Hajjaj, who said: "O son of Al-Akwa', you have turned back on your heels (i.e., reverted to Bedouin life)!" He said: "No, but the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) gave me permission to live in the desert."
1241: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah: A man said to the Prophet (ﷺ) on the day of Uhud, "What do you think, if I am killed, where shall I be?" He said, "In Paradise." So the man threw away some dates which were in his hand, and then fought until he was killed.
1160: Narrated Anas (رضي الله عنه): A man used to give the Prophet (ﷺ) some palm trees, until he conquered Quraizah and An-Nadir, and then my family ordered me to go to the Prophet (ﷺ) and ask him for those (trees) which they had given him, or some of them. The Prophet (ﷺ) had given them (i.e. that man's share) to Umm Aiman. So Umm Aiman came and put a garment around my neck, saying, "No! By Him besides Whom there is no other God, he will not give them to you, for he has already given them to me!" or as she said. The Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying, "You may have such and such (instead)," but she kept saying, "No, by Allah," until he gave her ten times as much, or as he said.
1144: Narrated Abu Qatadah (رضي الله عنه): We went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in the year of Hunain. When we met the enemy, the Muslims suffered a setback and turned back in retreat. Then I saw a man from the polytheists who had overpowered a man from the Muslims, so I turned around until I came upon him from behind, and I struck him with my sword on the tendon of his shoulder. He turned towards me and gripped me in an embrace so tight that I sensed the smell of death from it, but then death overtook him and he released me. I then caught up with 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and said, "What is the matter with the people?" He said, "It is the Decree of Allah." Then the people returned (to the battle), and the Prophet (ﷺ) sat down and said, "Whoever kills a slain enemy and has proof of it, the belongings of the slain shall be his." I stood up and said, "Who will testify for me?" Then I sat down. He again said, "Whoever kills a slain enemy and has proof of it, the belongings of the slain shall be his." I stood up and said, "Who will testify for me?" Then I sat down. He said it a third time in the same manner. Then a man said, "He has spoken the truth, O Messenger of Allah, and the belongings of the slain are with me, so satisfy him on my behalf." Abu Bakr As-Siddiq (رضي الله عنه) said, "No, by Allah! He will not give you the belongings of one of the lions of Allah who fights for the sake of Allah and His Messenger (ﷺ)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "He (Abu Bakr) has spoken the truth," and so he gave it to me. I sold the coat of mail, and with its price I bought a garden in the land of Banu Salimah, and that was the first property I acquired in Islam.
1201: Narrated Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) stood up among us and mentioned misappropriation (of booty), and he described it as a grave matter and emphasized its seriousness. He said: "Let me not find any one of you on the Day of Resurrection carrying on his neck a sheep that bleats, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I have no power to help you; I had already conveyed (the warning) to you.' Or carrying on his neck a horse that neighs, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I have no power to help you; I had already conveyed (the warning) to you.' Or carrying on his neck a camel that grunts, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I have no power to help you; I had already conveyed (the warning) to you.' Or carrying on his neck gold and silver, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I have no power to help you; I had already conveyed (the warning) to you.' Or carrying on his neck garments that flutter, saying: 'O Messenger of Allah, help me!' And I will say: 'I have no power to help you; I had already conveyed (the warning) to you.'"
1252: Narrated Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) never used to come upon his family unexpectedly at night; he would not enter (upon them) except in the morning or in the evening.
1211: Narrated Hudhaifa bin Al-Yaman: The people used to ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) about good, but I used to ask him about evil for fear that it might overtake me. So I said, "O Messenger of Allah, we were in ignorance and evil, and then Allah brought us this good; will there be any evil after this good?" He said, "Yes." I said, "Will there be any good after that evil?" He said, "Yes, but it will have some impurity in it." I said, "What will be its impurity?" He said, "There will be people who will guide others according to principles other than my Sunnah; you will see in their deeds both good and evil." I said, "Will there be any evil after that good?" He said, "Yes, there will be callers who call towards the gates of Hell, and whoever answers their call, they will throw him into it." I said, "O Messenger of Allah, describe them for us." He said, "They will be from our own people and will speak our language." I said, "What do you order me to do if that should overtake me?" He said, "Stick to the group of the Muslims and their leader." I said, "If they have neither a group nor a leader?" He said, "Then isolate yourself from all those different sects, even if you have to bite on the root of a tree until death overtakes you while you are in that state."
1263: Narrated Abu Tha'labah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the eating of the flesh of domestic donkeys.
1262: Narrated 'Ali bin Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him): That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade Mut'ah (temporary marriage) of women on the day of Khaibar, and forbade the eating of the flesh of domestic donkeys.
1253: Narrated Jabir bin 'Abdullah: We returned with the Prophet (ﷺ) from a military expedition, and when we set out to enter (Al-Madinah), he said, "Wait so that you may enter at night (i.e. in the evening), so that the unkempt woman may comb her hair and the woman whose husband has been away may shave her pubic hair."
1271: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "As for the mastigure (lizard), I do not eat it, but I do not declare it unlawful."
1256: Narrated 'Adi bin Hatim (may Allah be pleased with him): I asked the Prophet (ﷺ) about the mi'rad (a sharp-edged wooden hunting tool), and he said: "If it strikes the game with its sharp edge, then eat it; but if it strikes with its broad side, then do not eat it, for it is (killed by) a blunt blow." I said: O Messenger of Allah, I send forth my dog and mention Allah's Name, and then I find with it another dog upon the game over which I did not mention Allah's Name, and I do not know which of them caught it. He said: "Do not eat it, for you mentioned Allah's Name only over your own dog, and you did not mention it over the other."
1266: Narrated Al-Bara' and 'Abdullah bin Abi Awfa: They were with the Prophet (ﷺ) and they got hold of some donkeys and cooked them. Then the announcer of the Prophet (ﷺ) called out: "Turn the pots upside down (i.e., pour out their contents)."
1267: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): I do not know whether the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the meat of domestic donkeys on the Day of Khaibar because they were used by the people as beasts of burden and he disliked that their means of transport should be lost, or whether he made it unlawful.
1274: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: Umm Hufaid, the maternal aunt of Ibn 'Abbas, presented to the Prophet (ﷺ) some dried yogurt, ghee (clarified butter), and lizards (mastigures). The Prophet (ﷺ) ate the dried yogurt and the ghee, but left the lizard, feeling disgust for it. Ibn 'Abbas said: It was eaten at the table of Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and had it been unlawful, it would not have been eaten at the table of Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).
1316: Narrated Abu Qatadah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "When any one of you drinks, let him not breathe into the vessel."
1290: Narrated Salamah bin Al-Akwa': The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Whoever among you sacrifices an animal should not keep anything of it (i.e., its meat) in his house after the third day." When the next year came, the people said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall we do as we did last year?" He said, "Eat, feed others, and store up, for that year the people were in a state of hardship, and I wanted you to help (them) with it."
1333: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The food of two persons is sufficient for three, and the food of three persons is sufficient for four."
1318: Narrated Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to us in this house of ours and asked for something to drink. So we milked a ewe of ours for him, and then I mixed it with water from this well of ours, and I gave it to him, while Abu Bakr was on his left, 'Umar was facing him, and a Bedouin was on his right. When he finished, 'Umar said: "This is Abu Bakr (pointing to him, expecting the Prophet to give him next)." But he gave the drink to the Bedouin, then said: "The right side, the right side (should be given precedence); so give precedence to the right side." Anas said: "So it is a Sunnah, so it is a Sunnah, so it is a Sunnah," (repeating it) three times.
1326: Narrated Jabala: We were in Madinah among some of the people of Iraq, and a famine year befell us. Ibn az-Zubair used to provide us with dates as sustenance, and Ibn 'Umar would pass by us and say: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade combining two dates together (while eating), unless a man asks permission of his brother."
1346: Narrated Qatadah: I said to Anas: "Which garment was most beloved to the Prophet (ﷺ)?" He said: "The Hibarah (a striped garment made in Yemen)."
1321: Narrated Abu Mas'ud: A man from the Ansar, known as Abu Shu'aib, came and said to his slave who was a butcher, "Prepare for me enough food to serve five people, for I want to invite the Prophet (ﷺ) along with four others, as I have noticed signs of hunger on his face." So he invited them, but another man came along with them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said (to Abu Shu'aib), "This man has followed us, so if you wish you may permit him, and if you wish he may go back." Abu Shu'aib said, "No, rather I give him permission (to stay)."
1385: Narrated Abu Huraira: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The most despicable name in the sight of Allah is (that of) a man who calls himself Malik al-Amlak (King of kings)."
1353: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a ring made of gold, and he used to wear it with its stone turned towards the inside of his palm. So the people also made similar rings for themselves. Then he sat on the pulpit and took it off, saying: "I used to wear this ring and turn its stone inward." Then he threw it away and said: "By Allah, I will never wear it again." So the people also threw away their rings.
1395: Narrated Abu Huraira: that he heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "If someone peeps into your house without your permission, and you throw a pebble at him and put out his eye, there would be no sin on you."
1410: Narrated 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If you are three, then no two of you should whisper together excluding the third person, until you mix with other people, because that will grieve him."
1414: Narrated 'Aishah: Whenever the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to visit a sick person, or a sick person was brought to him, he used to say: "Take away the disease, O Lord of the people, and heal, for You are the Healer. There is no healing but Your healing, a healing that leaves no disease behind."
1423: Narrated Anas (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) used to get himself cupped, and he did not withhold the wages of anyone.
1407: Narrated Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her): The Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon me while a mukhannath (effeminate man) was with me, and he heard him say to 'Abdullah bin Umayyah: "O 'Abdullah, what do you think, if Allah opens Ta'if for you tomorrow, take the daughter of Ghailan, for she comes forward with four (folds of fat) and turns her back with eight." So the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "These should never enter upon you (women)."
1402: Narrated 'Aishah: Sawdah went out to relieve herself after the (verse regarding) veiling had been revealed. She was a large woman, and could not be hidden from one who knew her. 'Umar bin Al-Khattab saw her and said, "O Sawdah! By Allah, you cannot hide yourself from us, so think of some way by which you should not be recognized on going out." Sawdah returned while Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was in my house taking his supper, and there was a bone in his hand. She entered and said, "O Allah's Messenger! I went out to answer the call of nature and 'Umar said to me so-and-so." 'Aishah added: Then Allah revealed the Divine Inspiration (relevant to this incident) and then it was over, and the bone was still in his hand as he had not put it down. He then said, "You (women) have been permitted to go out for your needs."
1419: Narrated Um Salamah: The Prophet (ﷺ) saw in her house a slave girl who had a black spot on her face, and he said: "Seek treatment for her by Ruqya, for she is under the effect of an evil eye."
1426: Narrated Rafi' bin Khadij: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "Fever is from the heat of Hell, so cool it with water."
1404: Narrated Safiyyah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): She came to visit the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his I'tikaf in the mosque, in the last ten days of Ramadan, and she spoke with him for a while, then she got up to return home. The Prophet (ﷺ) got up with her to walk her back, and when she reached the door of the mosque, near the door of Umm Salamah, two men from the Ansar passed by and greeted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with salam. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Wait, this is Safiyyah bint Huyayy." They said: "Glory be to Allah, O Messenger of Allah!" and it was a matter of concern to them. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Satan reaches into man to the extent of his blood (i.e., he is present with him wherever he goes), and I feared that he might cast something into your hearts."
1440: Narrated Sahl bin Sa'd As-Sa'idi: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said, "If evil omen is in anything, it is in the woman, the horse and the house."
1459: Narrated Anas (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The true good dream of a believer is one of the forty-six parts of prophecy."
1432: Narrated Abu Sa'id: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "My brother has a complaint in his abdomen (i.e. diarrhea)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "Give him honey to drink." The man came for the second time and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "Give him honey to drink." He came for the third time and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Give him honey to drink." He returned again and said, "I have done that (but of no avail)." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Allah has said the truth, and your brother's abdomen has told a lie. Give him honey to drink." So he made him drink it and he became cured.
1444: Narrated 'Aishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ): That the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding the house lizard (gecko), "It is a wicked little creature," but I did not hear him command that it be killed.
1452: Narrated 'Aishah: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "None of you should say, 'My soul has become khabuthat (foul, wicked),' but he should say, 'My soul has become laqisat (uneasy, distressed).'"
1464: Narrated Abu Musa: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I saw in a dream that I was migrating from Mecca to a land in which there were date palms. My thoughts went to the possibility that it was Al-Yamama or Hajr, but it turned out to be Al-Madinah, i.e., Yathrib. In this dream of mine, I also saw that I brandished a sword, and it broke in the middle, and behold, that symbolized the casualties which the believers suffered on the Day of (the battle of) Uhud. Then I brandished the sword again, and it became better than it was before, and behold, that symbolized the victory which Allah brought about, and the gathering of the believers. I also saw cows, and by Allah, that was good, and they symbolized the believers on the Day of Uhud, and (the fact that they were good indicated) the good which Allah brought about, and the reward of true faith which Allah gave us after the Day of Badr."
1484: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "In front of you there is a lake as large as the distance between Jarba' and Adhruh."
1472: Narrated Abu Huraira: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying, "My similitude and the similitude of mankind is that of a man who kindled a fire, and when it illuminated what was around it, moths and these insects that fall into fire began to fall into it. He tried to drive them away, but they overpowered him and rushed into it. So I am taking hold of your waist-belts to keep you away from the Fire, but you rush into it."
1482: Narrated Haritha bin Wahb: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) mention Al-Hawd (the Reservoir), and he said: "It is as (the distance) between Al-Madinah and Sana'a."
1478: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Amr: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "My Lake-Fount is (so vast that it takes) a month's journey (to cross), its water is whiter than milk, its smell is sweeter than musk, and its drinking cups are like the stars of the sky; whoever drinks from it will never be thirsty again."
1465:
Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: Musailamah al-Kadhdhab (the liar) came during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) and began to say: "If Muhammad appoints me as his successor, I will follow him." He came to Madinah with a great number of his people. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went out to him accompanied by Thabit bin Qais bin Shammas, and in the hand of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) was a piece of a palm branch. He stopped before Musailamah, who was among his companions, and said: "If you were to ask me for this piece (of palm branch), I would not give it to you. You cannot escape the command of Allah concerning you. If you turn away, Allah will surely destroy you. Indeed, I see in you that which was shown to me in a vision, and this is Thabit who will answer you on my behalf." Then he turned away from him.

Ibn 'Abbas said: I asked about the saying of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ): "You are the one about whom I was shown what I was shown," (and was told its meaning).
1491: Narrated Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): I served the Prophet (ﷺ) for ten years, and he never said to me "Uff" (an expression of displeasure), nor did he ever say to me, "Why did you do that?" or "Why did you not do that?"
1471: Narrated Abu Musa: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The example of guidance and knowledge with which Allah has sent me is like abundant rain falling on the earth, some of which was fertile soil that absorbed the water and brought forth grass and abundant vegetation. Some of it was hard and held the water, and Allah benefited the people with it, so they drank from it, gave water to their animals, and irrigated their crops. Another portion of it fell on barren land, which could neither hold the water nor bring forth vegetation. The first is the example of the person who comprehends Allah's religion and benefits from what Allah has sent me with, so he learns and teaches others; and the (last example) is that of the person who does not care for it at all and does not accept Allah's guidance with which I have been sent." In another narration: "And a portion of it retained the water (in pools)."
1500: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Amr: The Prophet (ﷺ) was neither obscene nor did he seek obscenity. And he used to say: "Indeed, among the best of you are those who have the best manners."
1512: Narrated Abu Juhaifah (may Allah be pleased with him): I saw the Prophet (ﷺ), and Al-Hasan bin 'Ali (peace be upon them both) resembled him.
1510: Narrated Muhammad bin Sirin: I asked Anas, "Did the Prophet (ﷺ) dye his hair?" He said, "He did not reach old age (i.e., grey hair) except a little."
1508: Narrated Anas: The hair of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was wavy, neither straight nor curly, and it reached between his ears and his shoulders.
1504: Narrated Anas (bin Malik): Umm Sulaim used to spread a leather sheet for the Prophet (ﷺ) and he would take his midday nap on that sheet at her house. He said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) slept, she would take some of his sweat and hair and collect it in a small bottle, and then she would gather it in some perfume.
1513: Narrated As-Sa'ib bin Yazid: My aunt took me to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, my nephew is sick." He wiped my head and prayed for blessing for me. Then he performed ablution (Wudu'), and I drank from the water of his ablution. Then I stood behind his back and looked at the seal of Prophethood between his shoulders, which was like a button of a tent.
1514: Narrated Anas bin Malik, describing the Prophet (ﷺ): He was of medium height among the people, neither tall nor short. He was of a radiant (reddish-white) complexion, neither excessively white nor dark brown. His hair was neither curly nor straight. Revelation came to him when he was forty years old. He stayed in Makkah for ten years receiving revelation, and in Madinah for ten years. When he passed away, there were not twenty white hairs in his head and beard.
1516: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) remained in Makkah for thirteen years, and he died when he was sixty-three years old.
1517: Narrated Jubair bin Mut'im (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "I have five names: I am Muhammad and Ahmad; and I am al-Mahi (the effacer) by whom Allah effaces disbelief; and I am al-Hashir (the gatherer) at whose feet the people will be gathered; and I am al-'Aqib (the one after whom there is no other Prophet)."
1530: Narrated Abu Huraira (رضي الله عنه): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "We have more right to be in doubt than Abraham when he said: 'My Lord! Show me how You give life to the dead.' Allah said: 'Do you not believe?' He said: 'Yes, but to be stronger in faith.' May Allah have mercy on Lot; he sought refuge with a strong support (i.e. Allah). And if I were to stay in prison as long as Joseph stayed, I would readily respond to the call (of the one who called me to get out of the prison)."
1564: Narrated Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Who will bring me news of the (enemy) people on the day of Al-Ahzab (the Confederates)?" Az-Zubair said, "I (will)." Then he again said, "Who will bring me news of the people?" Az-Zubair said, "I (will)." The Prophet (ﷺ) then said, "Every Prophet has a disciple (Hawari), and my disciple is Az-Zubair."
1573: Narrated 'Ali (may Allah be pleased with him): I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say, "The best of its women is Mary, the daughter of 'Imran, and the best of its women is Khadijah."
1570: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar: Zaid bin Harithah, the freed slave of Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), we used not to call him but Zaid bin Muhammad, until there was revealed in the Qur'an: "Call them by (the names of) their fathers, that is more just in the sight of Allah."
1588: Narrated Anas bin Malik: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "The superiority of 'Aishah to other women is like the superiority of Tharid to other kinds of food."
1559: Narrated Sahl bin Sa'd: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to the house of Fatimah but did not find 'Ali in the house. He said, "Where is your cousin?" She said, "There was something between us and he got angry with me and left, and he did not sleep here." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man, "Look where he is." He came and said, "O Messenger of Allah, he is in the mosque, sleeping." So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to him while he was lying down, and his cloak had fallen off his side, and dust had gotten on him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) began wiping the dust off him, saying, "Get up, O Abu Turab! Get up, O Abu Turab!"
1553: Narrated Ibn 'Umar: When 'Abdullah (bin Ubai) died, his son 'Abdullah bin 'Abdullah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and asked him to give him his shirt in which he might shroud his father. He gave it to him, and then he asked him to offer the funeral prayer over him. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) got up to offer the prayer, but 'Umar got up and caught hold of the garment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, will you pray over him although your Lord has forbidden you to pray over him?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has only given me the choice, for He said: 'Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; (even) if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times...' and I shall increase it beyond seventy." 'Umar said: "He is a hypocrite." (Ibn 'Umar) said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) offered the prayer over him, and then Allah revealed: "And never (O Muhammad) pray (funeral prayer) for any of them (hypocrites) who dies, nor stand at his grave."
1603: Narrated Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him): I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "The Throne shook for the death of Sa'd bin Mu'adh."
1618: Narrated 'Urwah: I set about abusing Hassan in the presence of 'Aishah, and she said, "Do not abuse him, for he used to defend the Prophet (ﷺ)."
1614: Narrated Sa'd bin Abi Waqqas: I never heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say about anyone walking upon the earth that he was one of the people of Paradise except concerning 'Abdullah bin Salam. He said: And it was concerning him that this verse was revealed: "And a witness from among the Children of Israel bore witness..." (46:10)
1620: Narrated 'Aisha: Hassan asked the permission of the Prophet (ﷺ) to satirize the disbelievers. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "What about my lineage?" Hassan said, "I will extract you from them just as a hair is extracted from dough."
1635: Narrated Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Aslam, may Allah keep them safe; and Ghifar, may Allah forgive them."
1637: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Quraish, the Ansar, Juhainah, Muzainah, Aslam, Ashja' and Ghifar are my allies (Mawali), and they have no ally besides Allah and His Messenger."
1649: Narrated Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Do not abuse my companions! If anyone of you spent gold equal to Mount Uhud in charity, it would not equal a Mudd (a small measure of grain) spent by one of them, nor even half of it."
1640: Narrated Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): Tufail bin 'Amr Ad-Dausi and his companions came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Allah's Messenger! Daus (the tribe) has disobeyed and refused (to accept Islam), so invoke Allah's wrath upon them." It was said, "Daus is destroyed!" He said, "O Allah, guide Daus and bring them (to Islam)."
1656: Narrated Jubair bin Mut'im: that he heard the Prophet (ﷺ) saying, "He who severs the ties of kinship will not enter Paradise."
1639: Narrated Abu Bakrah: Al-Aqra' bin Habis said to the Prophet (ﷺ): "None have given you the pledge of allegiance except the thieves who rob the pilgrims, from Aslam, Ghifar, Muzainah and Juhainah." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "What do you think if Aslam, Ghifar, Muzainah and Juhainah were better than Banu Tamim, Banu 'Amir, Asad and Ghatafan - would they have failed and lost?" He said: "Yes." The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Him in Whose Hand my soul is, they are indeed better than them."
1622: Narrated 'Ali (رضي الله عنه): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent me, Az-Zubair, and Al-Miqdad bin Al-Aswad, saying, "Proceed till you reach Rawdat Khakh, for there is a woman there carrying a letter, so take it from her." So we set off, our horses galloping, until we reached the Rawdah, and there we found the woman. We said, "Bring out the letter." She said, "I have no letter with me." We said, "Either you bring out the letter, or we will take off your clothes." So she took it out from her braided hair. We brought the letter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and in it was written: From Hatib bin Abi Balta'ah to some of the pagans of Makkah, informing them of some of the affairs of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "O Hatib! What is this?" He said, "O Messenger of Allah! Do not be hasty in judging me. I was a man attached to Quraish but was not one of them (i.e., I was an adherent but not a blood relative), while the emigrants who are with you have relatives in Makkah who protect their families and properties. So, since I lacked blood relations with them, I wanted to do them a favor so that they might protect my relatives. I did not do this because of disbelief or apostasy, nor because of preferring disbelief after Islam." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "He has told you the truth." 'Umar said, "O Messenger of Allah! Let me strike off the neck of this hypocrite!" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "He was present at Badr, and how do you know? Perhaps Allah looked upon the people of Badr and said, 'Do what you wish, for I have forgiven you.'"
1671: Narrated An-Nu'man bin Bashir: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "You see the believers in their mutual mercy, love, and compassion, like one body. If one part of it complains of pain, the rest of the body joins it in sleeplessness and fever."
1681: Narrated Abu Huraira: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "None of you should point a weapon at his brother, for he does not know: perhaps Satan may cause it to slip from his hand, and he may fall into a pit of Fire."
1685: Narrated Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Jibril kept enjoining upon me kind treatment of the neighbor until I thought that he would order me to make him an heir."
1704: Narrated Ibn 'Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked about the children of the polytheists, and he said: "Allah, when He created them, knows best what they would have done."
1624:
Narrated Abu Musa (May Allah be pleased with him): When the Prophet (ﷺ) finished with (the battle of) Hunain, he sent Abu 'Amir at the head of an army to Autas. He met Duraid bin As-Simma, and Duraid was killed and Allah routed his companions.

Abu Musa said: He sent me along with Abu 'Amir. Abu 'Amir was struck in the knee by an arrow, a man from the tribe of Jusham shot him and fixed the arrow in his knee. I went to him and said, "O uncle, who shot you?" He pointed to me (indicating the man) and said, "That is the one who killed me." So I made for him and pursued him, and when he saw me, he fled. I followed him and kept saying to him, "Are you not ashamed? Will you not stand firm?" So he stopped, and we exchanged two blows with our swords, and I killed him. Then I said to Abu 'Amir, "Allah has killed your enemy."

He said, "Then pull out this arrow." So I pulled it out, and water gushed forth from it. He said, "O son of my brother, convey my greeting of peace to the Prophet (ﷺ) and tell him: 'Ask forgiveness for me.'" Abu 'Amir appointed me to be in charge of the people (in his place). He remained (alive) for a short while, then he died.

I returned and went in to see the Prophet (ﷺ) in his house, (where he was lying) on a bed of plaited palm leaves, with only a mat spread over it, so that the marks of the plaited leaves had left imprints on his back and sides. I informed him of our news and of the news of Abu 'Amir, and said, "He told me to say to you: Ask forgiveness for me."

The Prophet (ﷺ) called for water, performed ablution with it, then raised his hands and said, "O Allah, forgive Ubaid, Abu 'Amir, his sins." I saw the whiteness of his armpits (as he raised his hands). Then he said, "O Allah, on the Day of Resurrection, make him rank above many of Your creatures among mankind."

I said, "And (ask forgiveness) for me too." So he said, "O Allah, forgive the sin of 'Abdullah bin Qais, and admit him on the Day of Resurrection to a honourable entrance."

Abu Burda (the narrator of the Hadith) said: One of these two supplications was for Abu 'Amir, and the other was for Abu Musa.
1721: Narrated Abu Hurairah (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) said: Allah the Almighty says: "I am as My slave thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me. If he remembers Me in himself, I remember him in Myself; and if he remembers Me in an assembly, I remember him in an assembly better than it. And if he draws near to Me a hand's span, I draw near to him a forearm's length; and if he draws near to Me a forearm's length, I draw near to him a fathom's length. And if he comes to Me walking, I go to him running."
1690: Narrated Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: A woman came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, the men have taken away (all) your time (i.e., your teachings), so appoint for us a day of your own on which we may come to you so that you may teach us what Allah has taught you." He said, "Gather on such and such a day, at such and such a place." So they gathered, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to them and taught them what Allah had taught him. Then he said, "There is no woman among you who sends ahead of her three of her children (i.e., they die before her) but that they will be a screen for her from the Fire." A woman among them said, "O Messenger of Allah, (what about) two?" He repeated it twice, then said, "And two, and two, and two."
1757: Narrated Asma': She heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saying: "There is nothing more jealous than Allah."
1727: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Two words which are light on the tongue, heavy in the balance, and dear to the Most Merciful: 'Subhan Allahi wa bihamdihi, Subhan Allahil-'Azim' (Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him, Glory be to Allah the Great)."
1724: Narrated Abu Hurairah (May Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Whoever says: 'La ilaha illallah, wahdahu la sharika lahu, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu, wa Huwa 'ala kulli shai'in Qadir (There is no god but Allah, alone, having no partner; His is the sovereignty and His is the praise, and He is over all things Omnipotent)' one hundred times a day, will have a reward equivalent to that of freeing ten slaves, and one hundred good deeds will be recorded to his credit, and one hundred bad deeds will be blotted out from his record, and it (the recitation) will be a shield for him from Satan on that day until evening; and no one will bring anything more excellent than this, except one who has said it more than that."
1776: Narrated Ibn 'Umar (May Allah be pleased with them): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Allah will grasp the earth on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens will be in His Right Hand, then He will say: 'I am the King.'"
1787: Narrated Abu Musa (May Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is none, or nothing, more patient in bearing the harm that he hears than Allah. They attribute to Him a son, while He grants them health and provides for them."
1767: Narrated Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with them both): When 'Abdullah bin Ubayy died, his son came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said, "O Messenger of Allah, give me your shirt that I may shroud him in it, and offer the funeral prayer over him, and ask forgiveness for him." So the Prophet (ﷺ) gave him his shirt, and said, "Inform me when you are ready, so that I may offer the funeral prayer over him." So he informed him, and when he intended to pray over him, 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) pulled him back and said, "Has Allah not forbidden you to pray over the hypocrites?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I have been given a choice, for Allah has said: 'Ask forgiveness for them, or do not ask forgiveness for them; even if you ask forgiveness for them seventy times, Allah will never forgive them.'" So he offered the funeral prayer over him. Then there was revealed: "And never pray (funeral prayer) for any of them (hypocrites) who dies." (9:84)
1590:
Narrated 'Aishah: Eleven women sat together and promised and pledged to conceal nothing of the affairs of their husbands.

The first said: My husband is like the meat of a lean camel placed on the top of a mountain which is neither easy to climb, nor is the meat fat so that one might put up with the trouble of fetching it.

The second said: I will not disclose my husband's secrets, for I fear I shall not be able to leave anything out; for if I mention him, I will mention his faults and blemishes, all of them.

The third said: My husband is tall; if I describe him, I shall be divorced; and if I keep silent, I shall be left in suspense.

The fourth said: My husband is like the night of Tihamah, neither hot nor cold; neither fearsome nor tiresome.

The fifth said: My husband, when he enters the house, is like a leopard; and when he goes out, he is like a lion. He does not ask about what he has left in the house.

The sixth said: My husband, if he eats, eats too much, leaving nothing; and if he drinks, he drinks up all; and if he lies down, he wraps himself up and does not put his hand inside (towards me) to know my grief.

The seventh said: My husband is impotent, or foolish and confused. Every kind of ailment afflicts him. He may break your head, or wound your body, or do both to you.

The eighth said: My husband is soft to touch like a rabbit, and he smells sweet like the perfume called Zarnab.

The ninth said: My husband is a tall man with respect to the columns of his house, and long as to his baldric; his house is spacious, and his fire is often kindled for cooking or for guests, and his house is near the meeting place (of the people) so that whenever they meet, they will call on him.

The tenth said: My husband is Malik, and Malik is a wonderful man, far better than that. He has many camels with plenty of resting places (in his yard) but few pastures (i.e. he has many camels which stay near his house so that they may be slaughtered generously for guests, unlike those whose camels are away grazing), and whenever the camels hear the sound of the tambourine (or lute), they realize that they will be slaughtered (for guests).

The eleventh said: My husband is Abu Zar', and what do you know about Abu Zar'? He has given me many ornaments, and my ears are heavy with them, and my arms have become fat (i.e. I have become fat). He has pleased me, and I have become so glad. He found me with my family who were mere owners of sheep and living in poverty, and he brought me to a respected family who possessed horses and camels, and where wheat and grains were sifted (i.e. a life of luxury). Whatever I say, he does not rebuke or reproach me. When I sleep, I sleep till late in the morning, and when I drink water (or milk), I drink my fill. The mother of Abu Zar'! And what do you know about the mother of Abu Zar'? Her saddlebags were always full (of provisions for guests), and her house was spacious. As for the son of Abu Zar', what do you know about the son of Abu Zar'? He uses his mother's outstretched leather bed as his own bed, being as slim as an arrow drawn out of its quiver, and he is satisfied by eating the meat of a small kid. As for the daughter of Abu Zar', what do you know about the daughter of Abu Zar'? She is obedient to her father and to her mother. She has a fat well-built body which fills her garment and pleases her husband. As for the slave-girl of Abu Zar', what do you know about the slave-girl of Abu Zar'? She does not disclose our secrets, but keeps them, and does not waste our provisions, and does not leave the sweepings scattered around our house.

She (the woman) added: One day Abu Zar' went out at the time when the milk was being milked (from the animals), and he saw a woman who had two sons like leopards playing with her two breasts. (On seeing her) my husband divorced me and married her. Thereafter I married a noble man who used to ride a fast tireless horse, and he took a spear in his hand, and gave me many things, and also gave me a pair of every kind of livestock, and said, "Eat (of this), O Umm Zar', and provide for your relatives." She added: Even if I gathered together all the things he gave me, they would not fill the smallest utensil of Abu Zar'.

'Aishah added: Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) said to me: "I am to you as Abu Zar' was to Umm Zar'."
1808: Narrated Abu Huraira (رضي الله عنه): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your fire (the fire kindled by the sons of Adam) is one part out of seventy parts of the fire of Hell." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, that would have been sufficient (to burn us)!" He said: "It has been made to exceed it by sixty-nine parts, each one of them equal to its heat."
1831: Narrated 'Aishah: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "An army will invade the Ka'bah, and when they reach al-Baida' (a place in the desert), those in the front and those in the rear of them will be swallowed up (by the earth)." I said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will those in the front and those in the rear of them be swallowed up when among them are their marketers and those who do not belong to them (i.e., not part of the army)?" He said: "Those in the front and those in the rear of them will be swallowed up, then they will be resurrected according to their intentions."
1802: Narrated Abu Sa'id al-Khudri: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will say to the people of Paradise: 'O people of Paradise!' They will say: 'Here we are, our Lord, and at Your service.' He will say: 'Are you pleased?' They will say: 'Why should we not be pleased, O Lord, when You have given us what You have not given to anyone else of Your creation?' He will say: 'I shall give you something better than that.' They will say: 'O Lord, what could be better than that?' He will say: 'I shall bestow My pleasure upon you, and I shall never be angry with you after this, ever.'"
1846: Narrated Abu Huraira (رضي الله عنه): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "This tribe of Quraish will bring destruction to the people." They said, "What do you order us to do?" He said, "Would that the people kept away from them."
1836: Narrated Hudhaifah (رضي الله عنه): The Prophet (ﷺ) once delivered a sermon to us in which he left nothing untold, from that time up to the establishment of the Hour, but mentioned it - those who retained it in memory retained it, and those who forgot it forgot it. Sometimes I would see something which I had forgotten, then I would recognize it just as a man recognizes another man who had been absent from him, and when he sees him again, he recognizes him.
1837: Narrated Hudhaifah: We were sitting with 'Umar (رضي الله عنه) when he said, "Which of you remembers the statement of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about the Fitnah?" I said, "I do, exactly as he said it." He said, "You are indeed daring concerning it." I said, "The Fitnah of a man in his family, his wealth, his children, and his neighbor is atoned for by prayer, fasting, charity, and enjoining good and forbidding evil." He said, "This is not what I want, but rather the Fitnah which will surge like the surging of the sea." I said, "There is no harm for you regarding it, O Commander of the Believers, for there is a closed door between you and it." He asked, "Will the door be broken or opened?" I said, "It will be broken." He said, "Then it will never be closed again." We asked, "Did 'Umar know what the door was?" He said, "Yes, just as he knew that there is a night before tomorrow. I narrated to him a hadith that was free from errors." We were afraid to ask Hudhaifah, so we ordered Masruq to ask him, and he said, "The door was 'Umar."
1855: Narrated Anas (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "No prophet was sent but that he warned his nation against the one-eyed liar (i.e., the Dajjal). Beware, he is one-eyed, and verily your Lord is not one-eyed, and between his (the Dajjal's) eyes is written 'Kafir' (disbeliever)."
1863: Narrated Anas: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "I have been sent, and the Hour (i.e., the Day of Judgment) is like these two," and he joined his index and middle fingers together.
1860: Narrated Anas bin Malik (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no land but the Dajjal will tread upon it, except Makkah and Madinah, for there is not a single one of their passes but has angels guarding it, standing in ranks. Then Madinah will shake with its inhabitants three times, and Allah will expel from it every disbeliever and hypocrite."
1851: Narrated 'Abdullah bin 'Umar: 'Umar went with a group of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), along with the Prophet (ﷺ), to Ibn Sayyad, until they found him playing with the boys near the fort of Bani Maghalah. Ibn Sayyad had, at that time, almost reached the age of puberty. He did not notice (their presence) until the Prophet (ﷺ) struck him on the back with his hand. The Prophet (ﷺ) then said, "Do you testify that I am the Messenger of Allah?" Ibn Sayyad looked at him and said, "I testify that you are the Messenger of the unlettered people." Then Ibn Sayyad asked the Prophet (ﷺ), "Do you testify that I am the messenger of Allah?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "I believe in Allah and His Messengers." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "What do you see?" Ibn Sayyad said, "A true one and a false one come to me." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "The matter has been confused for you." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him, "I have kept something hidden for you." Ibn Sayyad said, "It is Ad-Dukh." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "Away with you! You cannot go beyond your limit." 'Umar said, "O Messenger of Allah! Allow me to strike his neck." The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "If he is he (i.e. the Dajjal), you will not be able to overpower him, and if he is not he, then there is no good for you in killing him."
1864: Narrated Abu Huraira (RA): The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said, "Between the two blowing (of the Trumpet) there will be forty." Someone asked, "Forty days?" He (Abu Huraira) said, "I refused (to say anything)." They asked, "Forty months?" He said, "I refused (to say anything)." They asked, "Forty years?" He said, "I refused (to say anything)." Then (the Prophet said), "Then Allah will send down rain from the sky, and they (the dead) will spring up (from their graves) just as vegetables sprout. There is nothing of the human body that does not decay except one bone, which is the coccyx (the small bone at the base of the spine), and from it the whole body will be reconstructed on the Day of Resurrection."
1872: Narrated 'Aishah: The family of Muhammad (ﷺ) never ate two meals in a day, but one of them was dates.
1886: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "A community from the Children of Israel was lost, and no one knows what happened to it, and I do not think it was anything but rats; for when the milk of camels is put before them, they do not drink it, but when the milk of sheep is put before them, they drink it." I mentioned this to Ka'b, and he asked me, "Did you hear the Prophet (ﷺ) say this?" I said, "Yes." He asked me this several times, so I said, "Do I then read the Torah?"
1891: Narrated 'Aishah: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to speak in such a manner that if a counter wanted to count what he said, he would be able to count it (i.e., he spoke clearly and distinctly, pausing between his words).
1887: Narrated Abu Hurairah: The Prophet (ﷺ) said, "A believer is not stung twice from the same hole."
1882: Narrated Usama: It was said to him: "Why do you not go to so-and-so and speak to him?" He said: "You think that I do not speak to him unless I let you hear it. I speak to him privately without opening a door (of dissension) of which I would not be the first to open. And I will not say to a man, even if he were my ruler, that he is the best of people, after having heard something from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." They said: "What did you hear him say?" He said: "I heard him say: 'A man will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and cast into the Fire, and his intestines will pour out in the Fire, and he will go around as a donkey goes around a mill. The inhabitants of the Fire will gather around him and say: "O so-and-so, what is the matter with you? Did you not use to enjoin us to do good and forbid us from evil?" He will say: "I used to enjoin you to do good, but I did not do it myself, and I used to forbid you from evil, yet I used to do it myself."'"
1888: Narrated Abu Bakrah: A man praised another man in the presence of the Prophet (ﷺ), so he said, "Woe to you! You have cut off your companion's neck, you have cut off your companion's neck," repeating it several times. Then he said, "If any of you has to praise his brother at all, let him say, 'I think he is such and such, and Allah knows best, and I do not vouch for anyone against Allah,' if he really knows that of him."
1897: Narrated 'Aishah: The verse "And whoever is rich, let him abstain, and whoever is poor, let him eat from it in a just manner" was revealed concerning the guardian of an orphan who looks after him and manages his property; if he is poor, he may eat from it in a just manner.
1895: Narrated 'Umar bin Al-Khattab: A man from among the Jews said to him: "O Chief of the Believers! There is a verse in your Book which is recited by you all; if it had been revealed to us, we, the Jewish community, would have taken that day as a day of festivity." 'Umar said: "Which verse?" The man said: "(This day I have perfected your religion for you, completed My Favour upon you, and have chosen for you Islam as your religion)." 'Umar replied: "We know that day and the place where it was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ). It was revealed while he was standing at 'Arafat on a Friday."
1904: Narrated Sa'id bin Jubair: I said to Ibn 'Abbas, "(What about) Surat At-Taubah?" He said, "Taubah is Al-Fadihah (the exposer), for it continued to say 'and of them, and of them,' until they thought that it would not spare anyone of them without mentioning him." I said, "(What about) Surat Al-Anfal?" He said, "It was revealed in connection with the Battle of Badr." I said, "(What about) Surat Al-Hashr?" He said, "It was revealed in connection with Banu An-Nadir."
1902: Narrated Al-Bara' (رضي الله عنه): This verse was revealed concerning us: The Ansar, when they performed Hajj and returned, would not enter their houses through their doors, but rather through the back. Then a man from the Ansar came and entered through his door, and it was as if he was reproached for that. So this verse was revealed: "It is not righteousness that you enter the houses from the back, but righteousness is that one fears Allah. So enter the houses through their doors" (2:189).
